utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around. This is case IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. All the accused are here. Prosecution, it's Mr. McCloskey, Mr. Vanderpuye, Ms. Soljan. Defence teams, I think everyone is present here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We expectedly found ourselves having to sit pursuant to Rule 15 bis this morning, I'm just putting it on record before we start. It is my pleasure today to announce that we have received news that Defence counsel Stephane Bourgon has been awarded by the Quebecois Bar Association one of the highest distinctions possible, namely that of advocatus emeritus. It is a piece of news that is sweet music to the Trial Chamber's ears. Our congratulations to you, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, any preliminaries? Do you have any distinction in the States, Mr. Ostojic, any awards?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, we do not, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are all ordinary.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Basically. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but that was by someone else. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning to all. I know there was a matter of tendering --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Your mic, I don't think your microphone is on. It is on now.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: There was the matter of tendering exhibits with respect to Dr. Parsons, and I don't know whether or not the Popovic team is prepared to proceed this morning. I am prepared to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I was coming first precisely to that. But apart from that are there any preliminaries? No. All right, Ms. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. Due to technical reasons we were unable to distribute the list. It is ready and we intend to distribute it during this session, and my apologies to my learned friends to the OTP for this inconvenience, but we shall be able to clarify this immediately at the beginning of the next session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If we have a next session. Thank you. Anything else? All right. The witness is here. Good morning, to you, Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Welcome back. I hope we will finish with your testimony as soon as possible, or the least time possible. Where were we? We still have to start with any cross-examination, but you haven't finished either. So let's continue with Ms. Soljan first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Soljan, my apology, but I don't think I did follow in full when you covered the -- some part of illogical connection. Could you cover that part again?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: I'd be happy to, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Now, you testified a few days ago that you recently reviewed a report concerning a person's tooth found at the Kravica warehouse.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And in it you also stated that that same person's body parts have now been found or identified in the secondary mass grave of Zeleni Jadar, meaning that a DNA connection exists --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: -- between Kravica warehouse and Zeleni Jadar?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes:

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Could we please have Exhibit 4525.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Do you recognise this exhibit Mr. Janc?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the report I was reviewing, report by Michael Hedley.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Could we go to page 10 of this report, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, could you please read out the portion of the text in this page which refers to the finding of the tooth.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is the second paragraph which starts "a fifth" -- which starts with: "A fifth visit was made to the warehouse on the 13th of October, 2000, and a detailed examination was made of the base of the entrance doorway to the right of the warehouse. Upon removal of the accumulated earth and debris, at this point a broken human tooth was found." And then we have this code next to it, KA01/110BP. And then: "In addition pathologist Dr. John Clark later confirmed its human origin."

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Janc, the number referred to, KA01/110BP, what is this number?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a number which was assigned at the -- for this particular tooth which was found at the spot. So number represent the particular -- particular body part found in this place.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And who assigns this kind of a number to your understanding?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These numbers are assigned always by the crime of scene officer. So who is conducting the crime scene investigation, this person is always assigning these numbers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. And how do you know this information?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know this information from the exhumation reports which I was reviewing because the methodology and the procedure is always the same, and also I'm familiar with these procedures, because it's a common procedure during the crime scene investigation that you are giving the sequent numbers for the certain evidence you find during the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Could we please have confidential Annex D? This is 4491. Not to be broadcast, please. And page 251. So this would be RO657797, or page 251 in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And Mr. Janc, could you locate -- could you tell us what this spreadsheet represents, please?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This spreadsheet represents not counted cases regarding the DNA connections. So -- and here we have a list with the names included.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And can you remind us why these cases were not counted by you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I explained, there were several reasons for that. One was being because there were connections between primary graves, Ravnice 1 and Ravnice 2. The second reason was being because they were related to the same group of graves within Glogova 2, so because we have several sub-graves in Glogova 2 and then we have connections between, for example, Glogova 2 and 8. And the third reason was because they were illogical in terms of how those connections would be found or connected between each other because, for example, we have primary grave which is not as disturbed, and then we have connection between the individual inside this grave and the individual which was found in totally different location or grave or secondary grave.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. And you had indicated on record when you last testified that the connection between the Kravica warehouse and Zeleni Jadar also appeared illogical to you in the beginning; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that illogical. The problem with this particular case was that I did not have enough -- enough information about what this KA01 represent. That was the problem with this particular case. So that's why I did not include this one in the connection chart because I did not know where exactly to put it. So but I did count this case separately.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. And if you look at this particular page on the spreadsheet, can you locate that number, KA01/110BP we just discussed?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can locate it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see it in the column case ID, which is the fourth column. So somewhere in the middle you will see this KA01/110BP.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Could we perhaps zoom in a little bit so we can see the first five columns more clearly, and in particular the middle portion.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can see this number now on the right-hand side which is attached to the individuals, IS.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And Mr. Janc, just to the right of this column, the case ID column, is -- we see a protocol number, and that's 10417/07, and the same protocol number is repeated two times below it. What does this repetition mean?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This repetition mean that there is a re-association so -- to the main case. In this case, main case was assigned to the tooth which was found at Kravica warehouse, and then later on, other pieces of the same individuals have been found in Zeleni Jadar grave.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. And in particular which Zeleni Jadar grave were they found in?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says -- just let my consult my report. It is in Zeleni Jadar number 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. And yet, Mr. Janc, the case ID for the same individual with the same protocol number indicates ZJA04. Can you explain what that means, if you know?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is site code which was assigned to this particular grave by the officer who was conducting the exhumation at the beginning of the exhumation. So this particular grave-site has a code ZJA04 SRE. So this is the code for the entire case, for the entire grave. Then you have numbers attached to this particular code, and this number means the particular -- this is a sequence number of the -- all the body parts or artifacts or whatever is found in the grave, so for example, you have number 2 here, and it means that this body parts were found as part of the evidence marked as number 2 in this particular grave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Soljan, where do we find that ZJA04?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, it would be in column 4, directly underneath KA01-110BP. If you see there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: -- are three same protocol numbers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: -- and the two protocol numbers -- or, rather, the two case IDs below KA01/110BP begin with ZJA04.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, you called this Zeleni Jadar 2, yet the number is ZJA04. Can you explain whether that's a discrepancy or not?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not a discrepancy. This number which you can see on the screen was assigned by the BiH authorities, and it is different than our numbers we were using before, so that's why -- and you can find the both numbers in my report, so in the table which I prepared, so you can find both numbers, so -- and you will find which particular grave is this referred to.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Could we please Exhibit 4990 [sic] at page 63, please. That would be X0194213. It can be broadcast. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, we had mentioned earlier, some illogical connections. Could you please point out on this spreadsheet one or more such connections that appeared illogical to you, and just explain briefly why, what made them appear illogical to you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And if we could perhaps zoom in again so that we can see at least the first four rows more clearly. Including the top, the very top, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. We can see the first line, the individual with protocol ID 8019/06. Here we have DNA connection between Cerska primary grave and Hodzici 2, that's the illogical connection to me which was explained already before.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Could you explain it one more time, though?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is connection between undisturbed primary grave and secondary grave Hodzici Road. So one individual was found in two locations, in these two locations. So that's what seems to be according to the information which I got from the ICMP update.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Could you go on to the next --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next one would be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second, Mr. Janc. While this connection should be logical, then how can one body part be found at -- in another site at all.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can explain a little bit more about it. That was when I was preparing and reviewing this stuff, these were connections which were, I would say, logical for me and for each -- and it is not possible that one individual is find in -- okay, it's possible but it is illogical. Let me explain. I was checking, for example, the autopsy reports for each and seeing every single body parts which is mentioned here. For example, Cerska, Hodzici Road 2 and Hodzici Road 3. And I found out, of course, because Cerska is primary undisturbed grave, that we have the entire body found in Cerska. And then in addition to that, we have also Hodzici Road and Hodzici Road 2 and 3, additional body parts found which wasn't illogical. And for this particular case, my assumption was when I was reviewing who are these individuals, that there were twins, and my conclusion was that probably there is a mistake. One of the brothers was found in Cerska, the other in Hodzici Road. And I was doing the same thing, meaning checking the autopsy reports for the all illogical connections which you can see here. And the same conclusions were found. So that body part of -- or same body parts of the individuals of the one individual were found, for example, in two different graves. So for example, you have two lower legs in both cases, so that was then also illogical. And because of that we have sent the question to the ICMP directly because they are the source of this problem, actually, to clarify these things. And they have just recently responded to us and with the response they basically agreed that there is most be probably mistake and they have explained why this mistake could have happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's go back to the one referred to in the first line. Do you know what it was that was found in Hodzici Road 2 and Hodzici Road 3?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't know from the top of my head exactly what was found there, but -- no, I would have to consult my -- the autopsy reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You said you assumed that those may be twins.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What is your basis of that assumption on your part?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My basis was that I have checked the ICRC missing list where I have found these two individuals, brothers found on that list, they were born on the same date. And I think that I've checked also -- for all of the cases I have checked the autopsy reports. But I cannot tell you exactly which body parts were found where now. I would have to consult the autopsy report again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In any event, your assumption started -- was based on your knowledge that the Cerska is the one that has been never been disturbed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was the basis for all of these cases which were illogical to me, but I did not exclude the possibility totally that this couldn't happen. That's why we consulted -- that's why I have checked the autopsy reports first and then also we were trying to get the clarification from the ICMP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can actually take him back to that very same page that we were looking at before at Annex D, it may also help clarify a little bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: So this would be page 251, and not broadcast, please, of 4491.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, can you see on this spreadsheet the case that you were just discussing or, rather, the connection that you were just discussing?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, this is the first four entries you can see on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And what was the basis of your assumption that it was brothers, that it could have been twins that had been identified?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, now you can see on the screen that they are referring to two names in here, so either of them was found in these two graves, so and they have assigned one protocol ID to both, so when I've checked those two names on ICRC missing list, so I found out that they are twins.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You said one protocol ID?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, one protocol ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But one with Rs.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can explain it. The most important is first part of the protocol ID which says 1 -- 8019, and then also slash 06. Without R, these are the main cases; with R, it means usually re-association to the main case, so it is actually reference to the same person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, proceed, Ms. Soljan.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And, Mr. Janc, going back to the case that we had just discussed, the connection, the body that was found both at the Kravica -- part of the body that was found at Kravica warehouse as well as Zeleni Jadar secondary grave, can we locate this connection in your chart at the end of Annex C?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And why is that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because at that time I was not aware of this connection, what this KA means.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Can we go to Exhibit P4490, page 65 of it, please. Perhaps we can just close in on the left portion of it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Janc, you had mentioned earlier that one case represents one connection?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: In the case of the Kravica warehouse to Zeleni Jadar or, rather, to two body parts in Zeleni Jadar, how many connections would that represent between the primary location and the secondary grave?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One connection.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One case.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. And let's, for example, focus on this chart. It shows there -- first of all, there are two lines that connect the primary grave of Branjevo farm in Pilica, a blue line with writing that says, "Soil, pollen samples, blindfolds, and ligatures." And then a red line that says, "20 cases." Can you just briefly explain what that means, what the difference between the two lines is?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the blue line represent the forensic evidence connections between those two sites. The red lines means the DNA connections.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Can we go to Exhibit 2996, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, are you familiar with this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And perhaps we could zoom out.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Do you know what this exhibit is?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. This is the map regarding Srebrenica mass graves showing the distribution of bodies between primary and secondary graves which was used by Dean Manning, and prepared by him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Could we have Exhibit 4524, please. And, Your Honours, we had distributed courtesy copies of this upcoming exhibit for easier viewing. Please let me know if you need another copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us what it is?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the map I prepared for this testimony, so it is the updated version of previous map.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And how is it different from the previous map?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Now, this one is related to DNA and forensic evidence connections. Previous one was just evidence -- forensic evidence connections map, so this one is related to both DNA and forensic evidence connections, and what is difference between this one and previous one, it's -- there are some new graves which were discovered lately or -- yes, lately, which you can find these graves on this map which are part of my report. And also you can see different lines, green lines which I can explain in detail.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Can we please close in on the upper part -- upper half of this map, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, can you explain what this upper half represents?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This upper half represent -- you have these red arrows which means the same as before, these are related to transportation of bodies from primary to secondary graves. So and now, then you have green dots which represent secondary mass graves. These red dots represent primary mass graves, and then have clusters around these green dots, so each cluster represents these areas of graves, for example, from Hodzici Road, Liplje and Cancari Road.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Can you explain specifically how the -- for example, how one set of secondary graves relates to a set of primary graves, or rather, what the map shows?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the map shows what kind of evidence or connections we have now that we can link these primary graves with secondary graves. So, for example, if you look into Orahovac 1 and 2, forensic evidence and DNA connections both link all the Hodzici Road graves with the -- this particular primary grave. And this is the same for all the others.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: With respect to, for example, the Orahovac or Lazete to Hodzici secondary graves, is there a direct DNA link between the primary grave and all the Hodzici Road secondary graves?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We have a directly link DNA link between Orahovac to all the Hodzici Road graves. But, for example, I think I will consult just briefly my report, because one number -- Orahovac number 1 ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In the meantime, Ms. Soljan, do you have copies available now?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, we haven't received them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have found it. So we have DNA connection between Orahovac 1 and Hodzici Road 5, actually we have seven DNA connections. Then we have DNA connections between Orahovac 2 with all the other graves on Hodzici Road.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means that body parts of the same individual have been found in both locations, so in primary grave and also in secondary grave.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you tell us what the situation is with respect to the secondary grave connection to the Petkovci dam?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the same situation here. We have DNA connections between Petkovci dam and - I will consult my report again - I think all of them. Yes, we have DNA connections between Petkovci dam and all the secondary graves in Liplje.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: How about the Kozluk primary grave?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the same. Although we don't have direct connections with all of the Kozluk graves -- with all of the secondary graves because number 4 and 6 were just recently exhumed, so we don't have any connections yet, but in respect to the others, you can find it in my report to which particular graves we have DNA connection established.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And Mr. Janc, you also have green arrows between one cluster of Cancari Road graves, Cancari Road graves 8 through 12, and the other cluster of Cancari Road graves 2 through 7, can you explain what that little green arrows mean?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This green arrow -- or all of them, all of those green arrows in this chart represent the DNA connections between secondary graves. So I found also two DNA connections between Hodzici Road and Liplje and also between different clusters of Cancari Road graves. So in ICMP March update you can find two connections between these two secondary graves.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What would it mean, Mr. Janc?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In case they are correct, and I will explain why I'm talking about that. We have two connections between these two secondary graves, and one of those was also on the list which was at that time illogical to me. So and that connection between Hodzici Road 5 and Liplje 2 was on the list which we have sent to the ICMP for clarification. So pending their response, we received the updated version of the -- updated version in March, and there was additional connection between Hodzici Road 2, 7 and Liplje 2 again. That's why I have included these connections into my chart. So we have received the response from the ICMP now saying that the first connection between Hodzici Road 5 and Liplje 2 is, I think, mistake. So when you have connections, I would say, between -- when you have just few connections between two sites, you have to be very careful about it to make any conclusion. When you have several connections, you can say that you have strong connections between two sites and you can conclude that these two sites are connected. Nevertheless, just let me finish this, if connection exist between Hodzici Road and Liplje, it shows again that most probably, or, you know, this is my conclusion, same transport means have been used when -- during the reburial, for example. So -- and that one site was contaminated. So body part, for example, stayed on the truck and then it was -- it was disposed into a grave on the other location. So it's not that illogical because we know that reburials in this area have followed each other, and it's possible that the connection between two sites can be established or found.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And, Mr. Janc, with respect to the Cancari -- connections between the Cancari grave secondary grave connections, you mentioned that when you have several connections you have a strong connection between two sites. utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, Mr. Janc, in your report --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Can we go back to the lower half of this exhibit, please.

utterances.text: Mr. Janc, can you explain what we see there?

utterances.text: Yes. First of all, you can see a lot of red dots around Konjevic Polje and Nova Kasaba so these are all new graves. And what is new in this chart you can see in small letters. So what is in capital letters, so that was already there before.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And where did you find out information about these new graves or newly added graves?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found this information on the exhumation reports which were provided to us by the BiH authorities.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And Your Honours, for the record, the various exhumation reports provide by the BiH authorities, those are Exhibits 4502 to 4523, and because of the massive amount of material I don't intend to go through all of those, but those are referred to in his report.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: So, Mr. Janc, can you then explain what we see in this lower part of the map?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, it's very similar then in the upper part of it. So you can see the red arrows showing the transportation of bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And now you can see we have some new arrows from -- going from Glogova to Bljeceva 1 and 2, 3, and Budak 1 and 2 which were not on previous map. And we know that these five locations are related to Glogova or actually to, yeah, they are secondary graves to Glogova primary graves, so. Then you have green arrows which represent -- which represent the DNA connections between secondary graves. And these are quite strong connections between, for example, Bljeceva and Zeleni Jadar graves, also between Budak 1 and 2 to Zeleni Jadar. So one individual was found, for example, in these two graves, or even three. And the last arrow, you can see it's a grey one, so that's the DNA connection we have established now when we were talking about just a few minutes ago, so DNA connection or between execution point Kravica warehouse and Zeleni Jadar grave.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Janc, in your report you also describe a connection between a primary grave and a newly exhumed secondary grave, and the connection is found based on a combination of ICMP data as well as exhumation report. Can you tell us a little more about that?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And can we go to page 17 of Exhibit 4490, please. That would be page 25 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, indeed I found this connection. And this is connection between Cancari Road 8 and primary grave Branjevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And can we please not broadcast. I don't remember if I said that already or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Cancari 8 -- Cancari Road 8 secondary mass grave was exhumed at the end of last year by BiH authorities. And when reviewing the exhumation report from these exhumation, I found the information within that there were identification documents found in that grave attached to the body which was marked as 065T. And you can see it, the description of this particular issue in Cancari Road 8 section of my report. So this particular individual or body parts of this particular individual have been found previously already in Branjevo farm. So the conclusion here would be that these particular individual have been found in two different locations, although we don't have the actual DNA report about it yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Can we please have Exhibit 4504.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this document is, Mr. Janc?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is exhumation report.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Can we zoom out, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For Cancari Road 8.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Where can you find this information?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see in the middle of the -- of that page in bolded text, site code assigned to this particular site was KAM 08 ZVO. And this particular site was related to Cancari Road 8.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And can we go to page 7 of this report. Not to broadcast, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, can you tell us what you see on this page of the document?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what I was talking about before. So you can see on the particular body which is marked with 065 T, and then you have description what was found, so the body without certain parts of it, together with the driving licence and identification document on this name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you know what that is? An identification document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's identification -- it's identification ID, usual ID for the person, "Licna karta."

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, he can also read out the portion that relates to the ID, and we can do this in private session so that the name can be said out loud.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. You can read it without the name.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: There is that option as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Could you read it without the name as well as without the particular address information if such exists?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So that I read out?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Just the relevant portion which identifies this individual.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just -- we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And Mr. Janc, when we were just looking at this connection between Cancari 8, Kamenica 8 and Branjevo farm execution site, there was a lot of red text in that portion of your report. What does the red text signify?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the red text is what is added in regard to Dean Manning's report. So this -- what you can see in this report in red text, that's what I have added in regards to the Dean Manning's report. All the rest what is in black text is part of Dean Manning's report.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And there are various ERNs that are referred to in that red text, what do they tend to refer to? ERN ranges?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These ERN ranges which are at the end of each text refers to the documents or the communication we have received from BiH authorities and are related to these particular grave-site so that you can find more information in this material.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And do you refer to these BiH documents throughout the report --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: -- in the same manner? So one final question on the connections issue, Mr. Janc. Do the numbers of DNA connections that you come up in Annex C in your report, do they effect the actual current overall number of Srebrenica victims?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is separate analysis done just to show how many connections we have, so it has nothing to do with the actual identification of the individuals.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. And based on your analysis of the March 2009 ICMP update, what is the current number of Srebrenica victims identified via DNA analysis in graves?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is 5.358. You can see it from the first page or actually second page of my report, and it is also repeated on the fifth page of my report. So you can find --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Can we go to Exhibit 4490, page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And what kinds of graves included in this count of 5.358 Srebrenica victims?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are all the graves we have any information on that these individual have been found in these graves. So this total calculation or number is related to all the mass primary and secondary graves, then those smaller graves which contains up to 10 individuals, and also individual graves.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. And Mr. Janc, you state in the report that the current number of the Srebrenica victims also includes 294 unique Srebrenica-related DNA profiles which have not yet been matched to a missing person. Can you explain what these unique profiles are?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The unique profiles are the individuals for which the DNA profile has been established already, but there were -- there was no DNA match established yet because the ICMP does not have a donor for this particular individual, so it means basically that we have confirmation that one additional individual has been found in particular grave but we just don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And were these unique profiles a part of the March ICMP update?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Can we just briefly go to Exhibit 4494A, second page. Second page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, what is this?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is sample page again of the Excel spreadsheet which was provided to us by the ICMP and it relates to the unique DNA profiles.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And do you know what the source case number and the target case number mean?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If we can simplify that that you can understand this, on the left-hand side you have source case number which basically means main case, and on the right-hand side you have target case number which would be re-association to this main case.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, you stated that your count of the 5.358 identified Srebrenica victims includes 294 unique DNA profiles, but at page 5 of your report, you note that the most recent ICMP update contained 304 unique profiles. Can you explain?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When we have this on the screen, yes, there were 304 unique profiles provided to us, so you will find on the left-hand side, which is source case number, on that spreadsheet you will find 304 such cases. So I have calculated or included only 294 of those cases and I will explain it why. Because nine of those cases were found in Bljeceva 1 and they did not have any connection -- the connection between -- the connection with the other mass grave or secondary grave was not established. So in case -- in those nine cases where you have only Bljeceva 1, I did not include those because Bljeceva 1 is mixed grave. So and until we don't get a name of the individual, we don't know actually if it is a Srebrenica victim or the victim of any other incident for which we know is part of Bljeceva 1 grave. So there have been a lot of individuals found in this grave which are related to the incident in 1992. So that's why I excluded or not counted those cases because you can't be sure about it, that they are Srebrenica-related victims. And there is one more individual which was found, or -- in Liplje 8, you will find it on this spreadsheet, the individual found in Liplje 8, and it's the only individual which was found there. And there I have the same problem because it's not coming out from the mass grave. We don't have any identifications already from this particular site that -- and the victims from this grave are Srebrenica-related victims, so I was not able to include this individual in total counting, so I exclude that one also.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Janc, how many graves were exhumed in 2008?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I know that there were five exhumations of secondary mass graves conducted in 2008.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And which graves are these?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are Zeleni Jadar 1A, Zeleni Jadar 1B, Cancari Road 4, 6, and 8.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And where in your report could we find this information?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can find the actual date of the exhumation in the table which is part of the first four pages of my report. So there you have exhumation date for each particular grave-site, and you can find this information there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Can we go to page 2 of Exhibit 4490, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, so can you just explain, then, what this table contains?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, you can see first column it is mass grave, then you have site code which was attached to this particular site, this particular mass grave, when this grave was exhumed. And the last two columns relates to the number of individuals so far identified from this grave. So first part of the column are the numbers which were used by Dean Manning, or are contained in his report. So and then you have the actual numbers next to it so that you can compare the increment.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. So, for example, if we look at your table at page 4, and we were looking at the results so far of identifications based on the exhumation of Zeleni Jadar 1B, what would we see?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For example, for Zeleni Jadar 1B, you can see that this site, this grave-site was exhumed between 7 and 18 of July, 2008, so in Dean Manning's report you have no individuals identified because at that time this particular site was not exhumed yet. Now we have already 21 individuals which are identified in this particular grave.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And if we wanted to see the list of these individuals, where in your report would we go for this?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have to consult the confidential Annex D where you will find all the individuals which are part of this grave-site, or any of these grave-sites.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And if we just briefly go to Exhibit 4491, page 150. Not broadcast, please. And the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Can you just explain to us what this is?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what I was talking about. So these are the individuals, 21 individuals which were found or identified from the Zeleni Jadar 1B grave. And you can see by the end last two entries, we don't have a name for these two individuals, so that means that these are unique DNA profiles. So whenever you see in confidential Annex D, this kind of entry, that means that these are related to the unique DNA profiles, so and you will always find them at the end of each spreadsheet, like here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And going back to your report at page 5, page 6 of the B/C/S, right up before the totals you include a category called "Others and Serbia related."

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And this is again Exhibit 4490, page 5, or 6, B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: What does this "Others and Serbia related" category mean, please?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, others are the graves or surface remains, individuals from which sites were also found in the ICMP 2009 update. And I was not able to make any conclusions so if these are the individuals found in the grave or surface remains, because we did not have sufficient or any information on these cases. So I have put it -- these 45 individuals in total in the table which is towards the end, to the end of Annex A. And then we have also 18 individuals which are related to Serbia. So when we consulted ICMP regarding these Serbia cases, what do they mean, they explained it to us that these are individuals which were found along the Drina river during the -- or after the Srebrenica events, and so they were recovered in Serbia. So both numbers, 45, those others and Serbia related, so together is 63 individuals so far identified.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, in the totals column for the data obtained by Dean Manning you have 4.238. Where did you obtain this number?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This number is coming out from his report.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. And specifically?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specifically last part of his report where he is presenting the numbers in the tables also as I'm doing here. So -- but he was in total calculation in his report, the beginning of his report is lower than you can see here for, I think, around 200 cases, but that's because Dean Manning was not confident enough to include Bljeceva-related and Budak-related cases into the total calculation, and also I think it's Sandici was also the problem for him because he was not confident that these are Srebrenica-related cases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Ms. Soljan, if I may go back to the number 63 that related to others and Serbia related, I wonder if those were -- Mr. Janc also has found some kind of connection, DNA connection with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, no. They all appear -- these cases appear on the ICMP -- ICMP update, so -- and what appears on this list are Srebrenica-related victims. So because we have the names of these victims, they are on ICRC missing list and we can say they are Srebrenica-related victims. That's why we have included those names in total calculation. But no connections we have because these are all, I would say, primary graves or surface remains which we don't have any connections between each other established.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The only reason they are included in this number is that they are included in the missing list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. And they also appears in the ICMP list which is related to Srebrenica cases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, why did you and your analysis of the ICMP data include grave sites such as Bljeceva 1 to 3, Budak 1 and 2, Sandici and others?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because now we have enough and sufficient information that these graves are indeed Srebrenica-related cases or graves, so individuals coming out from these graves have been identified and can be found on ICRC missing list. As well, we have much more documents and documentation related to these graves.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And what is the documentation related to these graves that you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring to the documentation which we received from the BH authorities regarding the exhumations of these graves.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. Very briefly, Mr. Janc, could you summarise the conclusions of your report regarding the total numbers of Srebrenica victims identified via DNA analysis on surface remains?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The findings regarding surface remains shows that in total we have now 648 individuals identified whose remains were found on the ground or on the surface. So it is part of Annex B of my report where you can find the description how did I find these numbers and what are the conclusions, so ...

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have Exhibit 3609, please. And page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us what it is, please?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is information which was sent to us by the BiH Commission on Missing Persons in the beginning of 2008 and includes the total number of the individuals collected on the ground, on the surface. So it is the information related to the surface remains collected between 1996 and 2007.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: If can we go to the next page, please. And if we can just zoom in on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, did you use this type of information?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: How?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have been using this spreadsheet or these spreadsheets which were attached to the report which were -- or to the information which we have just seen before. I've used it -- I've been using this a lot. So because what you have on these spreadsheets are the locations and site codes which were assigned to the surface remains during the collection. So, for example, you have second column in this spreadsheet where it says when the exhumation was conducted. Then you have the location where it was conducted. The municipality is the fourth row, and then you have the site code. And these codes are very important because you can find in the ICMP list these codes when they are referring to particular individual which was identified. So when I was making analysis regarding the surface remains, I was using this spreadsheet as a basis for my conclusions that particular individuals were found on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Can we have Exhibit 4501, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: What is this document, Mr. Janc?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is similar than the one we have seen before, but this is related to the exhumations conducted in 2008. So because at the beginning of 2008 we did not receive the data for the current year because the exhumations were going on, so we did receive this piece of information at the beginning of this year, so it relates to the exhumations conducted regarding the Srebrenica events in 2008. And you don't see just surface remains related exhumations. You can also find the mass graves exhumations which you can see from the column where it says the type of the grave, which says "vrsta grobnice." So when it says "povrsinski," it means surface, and then you have down there "sekundarna" MG [indiscernible], that means secondary mass grave.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And Mr. Janc, beyond analysing the ICMP data for the numbers of surface remains, were you able to draw any other conclusions concerning surface remains in your report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Beyond the numbers, do you draw any other conclusions at Annex B of your report?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Perhaps I'll simplify it. If we can have Exhibit 3901. Last page of this exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this is, Mr. Janc?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the map which was prepared by the BiH commission on missing person, and represent the distribution of the surface remains found between 1996 and 1998 in the area stretching south from the Potocari up to the north, so where the column was passing in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So and I have used or reviewing -- I was reviewing this map and also prepared the similar -- the similar conclusions regarding these three wider areas, so you can find in my report how many individuals have been found in different areas, so -- and I named them. You can see here on the south, this Pobuda area, where the most of them have been found. Then you have south-west of Zvornik, you have Snagovo area. And then you have north-west of Zvornik, Baljkovica area. So these are three main areas which are presented in my report where the surface remains have been found. Beside that you have also other areas because you can see on this map towards -- to the left where Vlasenica is, you also see some dots, so these are also surface remains and victims related to Srebrenica which were found in the other areas which are outside these three main areas. And I also included those from these places under the section "Other areas."

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Janc, are you aware of any errors or typos in Annex B of your report?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And this is 4490, page 44, English. Page 63, B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. You have in second paragraph, second line, the number 952. The correct number should be 957, as it is down in footnote number 2 where you have -- where you can see number 957. So this is total number of the surface remains cases collected on the ground so far. And also there is a mistake in the fourth line of the same paragraph where it says "See Annexure B." It should be, See confidential Annex D.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's time for the break. How much more do you have, Ms. Soljan?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: About five more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Five more questions. We'll have the break now. We'll have a 25-minute break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's continue, Ms. Soljan. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, at page 5 of your report, footnote 5, you note that the number of individuals identified as surface remains represents only profiles matched to missing persons. Now, why for surface remains did you count only the named profiles and not the unnamed profiles?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did not include the unnamed individuals which were found on the surface because of the reason I already explained before, so I was not that confident to include them or to consider them as Srebrenica-related victims. Because when these remains were collected on the ground, within these areas we have also victims from the other periods, not only 1995 or Srebrenica-related victims. So within these areas, the surface remains of the other individuals which are not related to Srebrenica events have also been collected. So until we have the name of the person which was found on the ground and we see that it is -- he is on the ICRC missing list, until that time we cannot include this particular person on to the total counting, so that's why I did not include those. And also at the time when I was preparing this report, I was not in possession of those unique profiles for the surface remains. So in the meantime, we received from the ICMP unique profiles at least for the surface remains, and I can say there is 25 individuals on those -- on their list which are related to the surface remains.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: But would you be able to say whether they are Srebrenica related or not? Would you add them to your count of 648?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's what exactly what I was just explaining, and why not. So we have those 25 individuals which we cannot say that they are Srebrenica related.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Can we go to Exhibit 4490, page 41 English, page 60 B/C/S, please. The ERN is X0194271 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, can you tell us what this table represents?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This table represents the calculation of total numbers of the individuals so far identified from different mass graves and secondary -- primary and secondary mass graves which are related to particular execution point.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. And the Defence counsel has been kind enough to point out an error in the spreadsheet. Could you tell us what that error is, please?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. It is error regarding Kravica execution point. The total number is 1.319. And we can say that this total number cannot be attributed -- all of them cannot be attributed to Kravica killing.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Can you describe in a little more detail what you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have prepared a corrigendum to this mistake and I have explained it there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Okay. Can we go to Exhibit 4492, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Sir, can you briefly summarise --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: -- the contents of your corrigendum?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this corrigendum, you can see the clarifications I have made regarding particularly to Kravica execution site that not all of the individuals can be attributed to this execution point for various reasons. Because we have evidence now or information regarding the grave L, which is part of the Glogova 1 grave where 12 individuals have been identified. We know their names, and for ten of them we know where they are coming from. So they were returned back from Serbia on 20, 24 and 26 of July in 1995. And then obviously somebody executed at this point in Glogova. So in this grave you have these 12 individuals. For two of them, I was not able to establish where those two individuals are coming from. So then beside that we have evidence and information that in Glogova graves are also the individuals which are collected from inside and around Bratunac school. Some individuals from Potocari. Some of them from Konjevic Polje and some of them from the Konjevic Polje-Bratunac road. So the total number is not correct. They are all not coming from Kravica execution point.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Did you need to clarify anything else regarding the final table of your Annex A?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can see, for example, for Branjevo I have clarified this is minor clarification. Branjevo execution point should be written as Branjevo/Pilica, because we know at Branjevo and related secondary graves there are victims which were killed in these two execution sites.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Based on your analysis of DNA identifications found in the March 2009 ICMP update, what is the current total number of Srebrenica victims in both graves and surface remains?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is 6.006 individuals.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Do you know whether any new exhumations are expected to take place in the coming times?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. I was just recently in contact with the BiH authorities. Actually, with the members of the Commission for Missing Persons, and they have informed me that they are planning exhumation in Mrsici village, which is close to Vlasenica, so where they have indications that some 15 to 20 bodies are buried. According to them, those are Srebrenica victims but we'll know for the fact when those individuals are exhumed. Then the other exhumation which is planned by them is going on in -- close to Bisina, actually it is in Bisina area, there is a cave inside which many of the individuals might be. So they have already went into -- they have already gone into this cave. Inside they have found some pieces of bones. They have taken them out, but because of the unexploded devices inside, they are not able to proceed at this moment. They are waiting for the experts to come to clean this area first and then they will proceed with the exhumation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Are you aware of any other exhumations?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, those are three mains, although we have pointed out to them one additional possible place in Bisina where the grave might be. So they are in process to testing this area, but I have no information regarding that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: And at this time have all the known secondary graves been exhumed, secondary mass graves?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not yet. There is Cancari Road 1 which is still unexhumed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: I have no more questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If I go back to that Glogova site. Mr. Janc said that he knows that individuals from Bratunac or Konjevic Polje, et cetera, were gathered and moved to Glogova. How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, these are conclusions based on the testimonies and statements given by the people who were involved in these proceedings, and they were also testifying here. And I have listed these names and their protected numbers regarding these events, what they were testifying about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So your conclusion is that although they are not -- they should not be included in Kravica killing but they should be included in Srebrenica killing overall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. That's the conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Judge Kwon, and I thank you, Ms. Soljan. Ms. Tapuskovic. Let me first try and see what to expect. How long do you think you will need for your cross-examination, Ms. Tapuskovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't think I will finish today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see. Okay. Thank you. And Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: One hour, Mr. President, approximately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. And Ms. Nikolic or Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: 15 minutes, if any, Mr. President, on Monday. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: As things stand now, it's, like, one hour and a half, maybe a bit more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very probably nothing. Maybe five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Josse?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Needless to say, nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Haynes?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'd like to reserve a small portion of time on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So there is a possibility we finish on Monday. There is a small possibility that we will finish on Monday. In any case you are always available, Mr. Janc, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Tapuskovic, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Janc, we have already met. It was on 16 April this year.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion we discussed some issues contained in your report and you provided me with explanations?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Those clarifications were recorded in an informative report that the Prosecution made available to the Defence teams; correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to make just one correction, perhaps. On the first day of your direct examination, it's on transcript 33381 in line 30, you said that Annex C is not confidential, in fact you said Annex D was not confidential, and Annex C was confidential. Can I just correct this to say that only Annex D of your report is confidential?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. Only the Annex D is confidential.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that one of your main sources for your summary was the ICMP list from March this year. On that list, as far as the Defence is able to see, there are 10.626 entries, some of them main cases, some of them re-associations; correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On page 2 of your summary when you were explaining the number of identified persons through DNA analysis, you said we had at least 5.358 identified persons. Tell me, what does this mean "at least"?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, what is meant is that there are still exhumations going on and identifications going on so -- but what do we have in the ICMP update which was provided to us is 5.358. This is the correct number and the exact number, so what I meant with "at least" is probably, you know, I have had in mind that there would be additional exhumations and that -- additional identifications, and that's what is -- what was meant by that.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We will now move on to the unique DNA profiles, that is, your statement that you have established the existence of 304 unique DNA profiles. But you told us today that you put in your summary only 294 DNA profiles; correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You also said that nine of the differences appear in ten profiles, you said that nine appear in the grave --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please repeat the grave. The first grave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Tapuskovic, the interpreters didn't catch the name of the first grave. In any case, we don't have anything in the transcript, so you need to repeat them all if you said more than one, you mentioned more than one. What we have is: "You also said that nine of the difference," and there is a mistake here or something missing, "appear in 10 profiles, you said that nine appear in the grave," you need to correct that by repeating the name or names that you mentioned, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I'll repeat the whole question.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, you said that out of those ten cases looks like the difference of between 304 DNA profiles, and 294 demonstrated DNA profiles, nine cases referred to the grave Bljeceva 1, and one to the grave Liplje 8?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You told us today that for Bljeceva as a grave, you have no information that it is related to any other grave. However, in it were also bodies from 1992?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was telling that for Bljeceva grave you have information that it is a mixed grave. That inside this grave there are also individuals from the other incidents from 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, tell me, how many such persons are buried in that grave, do you know the number? Or is it these nine, namely, the difference between the unique DNA profiles? Are these the persons buried in that grave who died earlier?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my information, it is - I will give you a rough estimate - around 50 of those individuals found in this grave which are not -- which are related to the 1992 incident.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your summary, but also in the Manning summary, Liplje 8 grave appears. The Manning summary is marked P2993, and it is mentioned that also one body was found. However, for that body you had no information about DNA analysis. Tell me then, why is the grave Liplje 8 again referred to in your report when it concerns only one body and there is no DNA profile and it is impossible to link it with the list of missing persons?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's because it's simply I did not want to change the Dean Manning's report in any sense, and this Liplje grave 8 is considered to be a grave with one individual inside, but we don't have sufficient information about him. So if this is the individual which is on this unique DNA profiles list with Liplje 8 markings, I don't know. I can't connect this individual with this particular grave.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So you cannot say about that person that it is Srebrenica related?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which person do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: The one in the Liplje 8 grave.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us, Mr. Janc, on several occasions during your direct examination you used that term, Srebrenica related. Can you tell us what do you understand that term, Srebrenica related, to mean?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means the individuals, the victims which were killed or which have died after the events of Srebrenica in 1995, so after they took over the Srebrenica enclave.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In response to a question by my learned friend you gave us an explanation regarding the status of the number of victims related to Kravica, and you said you modified it in your corrigendum Exhibit 4492. Can we agree that when we read this corrigendum of yours, we find that the total number is over 100 persons, persons who are included in your count of 1.319 persons who met their death at Kravica and who, according to your corrigendum, cannot be associated with the incident in Kravica in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I now call up in e-court 1D1391.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, here we have a report that the Defence received on the 27th of April this year from the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we zoom in a little so that the witness can see better.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, are you familiar with this report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now move on to page 2, item 4, that is bullet 4. And zoom in a little.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I will read out to you part of this point which reads: "[In English] Mr. Janc noted that a number of witness statements he has reviewed showed that at least ten individuals identified via DNA analysis from the Cerska mass grave may have been captured after 13 July 1995, in some cases as late as 17 of July. These men have case IDs: [Interpretation] Cerska 20, Cerska 30, Cerska 32, Cerska 36, Cerska 51, Cerska 65, Cerska 66, Cerska 83, Cerska 101, and Cerska 116." Mr. Janc, you reviewed the report --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Soljan.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I just want to make clear on the record I did not lead evidence regarding this particular issue because we were given the understanding that various Defence counsel were going to be objecting to it being led. So just to make clear for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: But we have no objection to it coming in, obviously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, I mean, especially if you knew beforehand that this is something that they were going to deal with, and it is important so there's no question about it. Yes, Ms. Tapuskovic, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours, let me just check if all the numbers have been recorded in the transcript. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, I presume that you have read Mr. Haglund's report from my learned friends, that's Exhibit P611, which refers to the Cerska grave?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: On page of this exhibit, which we are not going to call up, that ends with the digit 3698, he mentioned two more persons, that is, Cerska 12 and Cerska 82 who had been seen on the 16th and 17th of July alive. Are you aware of this piece of information?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not from the top of my head, but I think I do remember reading this, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that Mr. Haglund also stated that all the individuals found in the Cerska grave had been executed above or next to the very grave and that they had all been buried on the same day?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you then tell me how do you explain the difference that 10, and the Defence claims 12, persons in the Cerska grave were most probably killed much later than the 13th of July, 1995, when, according to the OTP and the indictment, approximately 150 people were killed in the afternoon of that day?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means that these individuals were killed later, not on 13, or that the Cerska killing or execution took place later.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But let me just remind you, on page 33392, during your examination-in-chief, you stated that Cerska was the primary undisturbed grave; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You also mentioned today when you spoke about Kravica that there's a number that cannot be included into the number of 1.319 people. However, you confirm now that a certain number of individuals cannot be included in the number relating to Bljeceva as well. And then again, you just now confirmed that a certain number of individuals cannot be counted as being executed as described in the indictment and that actually they were killed probably after the 13th, and were buried in a primary undisturbed grave.
